## Addendum L (2026-11-14; written BEFORE any run): round 6 — night mean reversion on FX crosses (MQL5 survey, idea 2)
The user asked to go on with the tests ("continue les tests pour améliorer"). This round tests the second idea of the
survey (`results/r2/mql5_survey.json`): the "night scalpers" that fade small stretches after the 17:00 New York
rollover. Best evidence: signal 'Scalp IC Markets ECN' (https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/683917), a real account public
since July 2020: PF 1.79, 70.5 % winners, average win 3.43 against average loss 4.56 EUR, average hold 2 h, rules not
published. A review of about twenty public sources (open code, articles, vendor manuals, live signals, one independent
Dukascopy test; notes committed with this text as `results/r2/round6/night_fade/sources.md`) found no published rule,
only shared elements. The rule below is their common core written as one computable rule with one parameter set for
every cross; where the sources disagree, the alternatives are the neighbours. It replaces the survey's placeholder
(M15 bars, 18:30–23:45, six crosses), which was never declared. Of the new price files only header lines and one first
row (eurcad-m1-bid-2013, to check the time unit) were opened, and before the download the lead printed two rows of a
one-week test download (EURCAD bid, March 2021) to check the tool's format; nothing was computed on any price. Every reading of a
detail left open goes into `declared.json`, with its sha256, before any return is computed.

**Frozen rule `night_fade` (the main configuration).**
- **Basket**: all twelve crosses fixed in `dl_round6.py` before the research: EURCAD, GBPCAD, EURAUD, AUDCAD, EURGBP,
  EURCHF, GBPCHF, AUDNZD, NZDCAD, CADCHF, GBPAUD, EURNZD. None chosen on results; no major pair (the idea and its
  evidence are about crosses; one data source and one cost model). A cross leaves only by the coverage pre-check
  below.
- **Data**: Dukascopy M1 bid and ask (`data/raw_r6`, the 216 files of 2013–2021, all on disk), merged exactly as
  `prep_round3._merge` with the weekday rule of `prep_round3.fx`; frames asserted to end before 2022-01-01 and read
  with the filter ts < 2022-01-01 (`data/r6/<cross>_m1.parquet`). One pip = 0.0001 for all twelve.
- **Evenings** (New York wall clock, `America/New_York`): E = a date from Monday to Thursday; it opens trading day
  E+1. Skipped: E from 24 December to 1 January; E or E+1 an NYSE full holiday (`idxus_lib.us_holidays` minus
  `SPECIAL_CLOSURES`; half days are normal). That leaves 1,753 evenings, 2013-01-02 to 2021-12-22 (194–196 a year).
  For each cross an evening is tradable once 480 completed H1 bars exist at 17:15 (warm-up: about the first four weeks
  of 2013).
- **Band**: M5 bars = `goldlab.data.bars(base frame, "5min")` (clock grid; a bucket with no M1 bar has no bar), mid
  closes. For bar j: μ = mean of the closes of bar j and the 19 existing bars before it, σ = their population standard
  deviation, bands μ ± 2.0 σ; usable only if bar j−19 starts at most 120 minutes before bar j ends.
- **Signal**: decision times = the ends of the 5-minute buckets 17:15, 17:20, …, 19:55 of E (33 a night); the signal
  bar is the bar of the bucket that ends then (none, or band not usable: no signal). Close below the lower band: buy;
  above the upper band: sell (strict). D = |close − μ|.
- **Cost filter** (the scale-free form of the maximum-spread filter almost every source uses, measured against the
  trade's own target; BG Robonight and Night Hunter Pro similarly require a minimum channel width): the signal counts
  only if D ≥ 2.0 × C, C = ask close − bid close of the signal bucket's last M1 bar (base frame: Dukascopy spread plus
  commission).
- **Entry**: at market at the open of the first M1 bar starting at or after the decision time; dropped if that bar
  starts more than 5 minutes late, or if its open has already reached the target (buy: ask open ≥ μ; sell: bid
  open ≤ μ; a trade server refuses such a take-profit). A dropped order does not block later signals. A buy fills at
  the ask open + 0.1 bp, a sell at the bid open − 0.1 bp.
- **Exits** (`goldlab.sim.simulate` on M1 bid/ask highs and lows; stop first when both are touched in one bar).
  *Target* = μ of the signal bar, frozen, a resting limit with no slippage (a long exits when a bar's bid high reaches
  it, a short when a bar's ask low does; possible on the entry bar). *Stop* = 2.0 × the mean (mid high − mid low) of
  the 480 most recent completed H1 bars at the decision time (`bars(base frame, "1h")`;
  completed = start + 60 min ≤ decision time), set from the fill and fixed, 0.3 bp of slippage, the worse open on a
  gap. *Time* = at market at the open of the first M1 bar at or after 21:00 New York (`exit_index`, 30-minute gap
  rule), 0.1 bp. No trade crosses 17:00 New York, so the swap is 0 (asserted).
- **Positions**: one per cross (`no_overlap=True`: an order whose entry bar is at or before the open trade's exit bar
  is ignored); later signals of the evening may trade, on either side; no cap across crosses or per currency
  (reported). R = side × (exit fill − entry fill) / |entry fill − stop|.

**Costs.**
- **Base**: Dukascopy's own minute bid and ask, unclipped (each night's real widening, rollover tails included), plus
  FP Markets Raw commission, 6 USD per 100,000 units of base round trip, folded into the quotes (bid − h and ask + h
  on all four prices, h = ½ × c × the M1 bar's mid close) at fixed low-end USD values of the base (EUR 1.05, GBP 1.20,
  AUD 0.65, NZD 0.60, CAD 0.70; general knowledge, not measured, so the commission is if anything overstated):
  c = 0.5714 bp for the five EUR crosses, 0.5000 bp for the three GBP crosses, 0.9231 bp for AUDCAD and AUDNZD,
  1.0000 bp for NZDCAD and 0.8571 bp for CADCHF. Slippage 0.1 bp on market fills, 0.3 bp on stops, none on targets.
  Why not an FP spread model: FP's cross spreads are not verified, and its intraday shape clipped at 6 × the daily
  median would understate the minutes after 17:00. Known bias: Dukascopy's cross spreads were wider in 2013–2015 than
  ECN spreads are today.
- **Costs × 1.5** (base spread × 1.5 around the mid with `apply_spread_mult`, slippage × 1.5), two readings that must
  both pass: (a) orders rebuilt on the widened quotes (the lab's stress; the filter then sees 1.5 C); (b) the base
  orders replayed unchanged. **Gross** (information): the base orders on mid quotes, no slippage.

**Neighbours (each changes one thing; all logged; 7 configurations with the main).** (1) `first_hour`: decisions
17:15–17:55 (the hour the only independent test calls the core). (2) `moving_mid`: the same orders without a resting
target; exit at market at the open of the first M1 bar at or after the end of the first usable M5 bar that ends after
the entry bar starts and whose mid close is ≥ (long) / ≤ (short) its own middle band; stop and 21:00 exit unchanged.
(3) `width_2.5`: bands ± 2.5 σ. (4) `m15`: M15 bars (span limit 360 minutes), decisions at the ends of the 15-minute
buckets 17:15–19:45. (5) `stop_3.0`: stop 3.0 × the mean H1 range. (6) `one_per_night`: only the first order of each
cross and evening.

**In sample only (2013–2021), frames cut while read. The verdict is read on the main only; pass = all twelve bars:**
n ≥ 250; pooled PF ≥ 1.12; t on daily sums of R ≥ 2.5 (trading day of entry, days with a trade); at least 6 of the 9
calendar years positive (entry year; a year with no trade is not positive); pooled PF ≥ 1.04 at costs × 1.5 in both
readings; at least 8 of the 12 crosses with a positive expectancy (no trade = not positive); no cross above 25 % of
the pooled net R (a pooled total ≤ 0 fails); median pooled PF of the six neighbours ≥ 1.06; every-signal
expectancy > 0 (every order of the main, overlaps allowed); max hold ≤ 5 trading days; null ≥ 97.5th percentile;
|weekly correlation with the sum of the ten| ≤ 0.30.
- **Before the run (no return computed)**: a pre-check (frames, evenings, warm-up, signals and drops per
  configuration, spreads and all-in costs by cross and year at 17:15–21:00 and 16:55–17:30, the clock in UTC in both
  daylight-saving regimes); a cross with an M1 bar in [17:15, 21:00) on fewer than 90 % of the 1,753 evenings is
  dropped (the cross bars then apply to the crosses kept, 65 % rounded up); a synthetic test; a truncation test (μ, σ,
  side, D, C and the stop distance of at least 50 decisions per cross, recomputed on frames cut at the decision time,
  must be equal); a hand check from the raw quotes of the first main trade of 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2021.
- **Null** (section 4: same clock time, random day, same instrument): 200 replays, numpy `default_rng(0)`. Each main
  trade is re-entered on its cross, on an evening drawn uniformly with replacement among the cross's tradable
  evenings, at the open of the first M1 bar at or after the New York clock time of its entry bar (another evening if
  that bar is more than 5 minutes late; after 20 draws dropped and counted); same side; stop and target distances as
  fractions of its entry fill, scaled by the replay bar's mid open; resting target; time exit at 21:00 New York of
  that evening; base costs; every replay simulated (`no_overlap=False`). Statistic: the pooled mean R;
  percentile = share of the 200 means strictly below the main's.
- **Correlation**: Addendum K's convention (the ten's official trades read with entry_time < 2022-01-01, exits in 2022
  dropped; weekly R by exit week, W-SUN UTC, every week from 2014-01-01 to 2021-12-31 (418), an empty week = 0;
  Pearson).
- **Reported, not judged**: for every configuration, pooled and per cross: n, PF, t on daily sums and on trades,
  expectancy, R by year, long and short, win rate, average win and loss in R and their ratio (683917: 70.5 % winners,
  0.75), exits by reason, hold, net, gross and cost bp, target and stop distances in pips, all also at costs × 1.5
  (both readings) and gross. For the main: entries by New York hour, weekday and daylight-saving regime; first against
  later trades of the evening; drops by filter; evenings skipped by reason and cross; entries, stops and targets
  between 16:55 and 17:30; stop and target in one M1 bar; × 1.5 fills already past the target; expectancy by D / C
  (2–3, 3–4, ≥ 4); the AUD and NZD crosses against the other six; winning days, weeks and months; worst evening and
  week; maximum drawdown in R; crosses open at once and the most trades open on one currency and side; the account
  check at 7 % of 1,000 EUR (0.01 lot, 1:500); the break-even extra cost per round trip; the evenings of 2016-10-06
  (pound flash crash, about 19:07) and 2019-01-02 (yen and Australian-dollar flash crash, about 17:30–17:45), the week
  of 2021-11-22 and EURCHF before 2015-01-15, all of which stay in the test.
- **Bookkeeping**: `results/r2/round6/night_fade/trials.jsonl`, one line per configuration and cross plus one pooled
  line per configuration (91), whatever the result; the run refuses to run twice; `results/val_access.log` unchanged.
- **After the run**: a fail is final (another window, band, stop, filter, bar size or cross list is a new idea with
  its own declaration). A pass is attacked by an independent re-implementation (own frames, calendar, bands, H1 ranges
  and simulator; trade for trade; execution on the 1,000 EUR account). A confirmed pass gets ONE look at 2022–2025,
  declared separately; the crosses' 2022–2025 files are downloaded only after that declaration. Before any real use:
  FP's night quotes on the twelve crosses are read with `ReleveFP` v1.10 (InpSymbols = the twelve crosses,
  InpDays = 45: at least 20 Monday–Thursday evenings, a second run a month later if fewer) and the commission from a
  demo round trip; a cross whose FP median all-in cost over 17:15–21:00 New York exceeds 1.5 × the base frame's median
  at the same minutes over 2019–2021 is not traded; with fewer than 8 crosses left the rule is not used; then the demo
  account first. The 2026 holdout stays untouched.

**Said before the run.** The vendors' records are better than this test can be: they rest limit orders at the band (no
spread paid to enter), tune per pair, use low-spread ECN brokers and are survivors (22 of the 26 signal links on their
pages are gone); the lab enters at market after the bar closes and crosses the spread. Arithmetic: under the filter a
target win nets D − C/2 ≥ 0.75 D, with a stop several times D, so of the order of +0.1 to +0.4 R against losses up to
−1 R; PF 1.12 needs a net mean of about 5.7 % of the mean |R|. The lab's FX record: no FX rule among the ten;
round 3's FX edges were 1–2 bp gross at best; round 4's FX weekend fade had no gross edge (−0.19 bp per trade before
costs). Expected: a few thousand to about 15,000 trades, 60–75 % winners, a gross PF above 1 and, if it fails, failing
on PF, costs × 1.5 and years; the null can pass even then (it tests timing, not costs). Prior of an in-sample pass
about 8 %, of a later 2022–2025 pass about 3 %; |ρ| with the ten below 0.1. If it passed: a small sleeve on a clock
and a market the ten never touch, not a multiplier; at 7 % per trade a per-evening risk budget would be declared
before any real use.

costs.base_quotes: Dukascopy M1 bid and ask, unclipped, merged as prep_round3._merge (data/r6 frames)
costs.commission_fold: h = 0.5 x c x 1e-4 x (bc + ac) / 2 of the same M1 bar; bid - h and ask + h on o, h, l, c

readings.a: orders rebuilt on the widened frame

configurations.name: moving_mid
configurations.role: neighbour (2): no resting target; market exit after the first M5 close back at its own middle band

configurations.name: m15
configurations.role: neighbour (4): M15 bars, span limit 360 minutes, decisions 17:15-19:45

configurations.name: stop_3.0
configurations.role: neighbour (5): stop 3.0 x the mean H1 range

configurations.name: one_per_night
configurations.role: neighbour (6): only the first order of each cross and evening

readings_of_open_details.L1_in_sample_frames: Frames are built by frames.py from the 216 files of data/raw_r6 (2013-2021; no later file exists for the crosses). Each file is read with pyarrow.dataset and the row filter timestamp < 2022-01-01 00:00 UTC inside the read call (to_table(filter=...)); bid and ask are merged by prep_round3._merge itself (imported; its _read is replaced at call time by a reader with _read's semantics plus the filter: files in sorted order, duplicates keep the first, sorted), then prep_round3.fx's weekday rule ((New York time + 7 h).dayofweek < 5) is applied; the frame is written to data/r6/<cross>_m1.parquet. Every later read uses pandas.read_parquet(filters=[('ts', '<', 2022-01-01 UTC)]) and asserts max(ts) < 2022-01-01. goldlab.r2.load/run/evaluate/null_test and r2/tracks/fx/common.load_is are never used (whole-file reads; r2.costs has no crosses): the run calls goldlab.sim.simulate directly. The hand check reads the raw csv.gz with Python's csv module and skips rows >= 2022-01-01 in its read loop. results/val_access.log is hashed before and after the run and must be unchanged; lab/holdout_raw is never opened.
readings_of_open_details.L2_base_frame: The base frame is not stored: common.load_base builds it in memory from the merged frame: h = 0.5 x c x 1e-4 x (bc + ac) / 2 of the same M1 bar (before folding), bid - h and ask + h on open, high, low and close; c in bp of price round trip exactly as listed (0.5714 for the five EUR crosses, 0.5000 for the three GBP crosses, 0.9231 for AUDCAD and AUDNZD, 1.0000 for NZDCAD, 0.8571 for CADCHF). Every decision quantity (bars, bands, D, C, the refused-target check, H1 ranges) and every base fill is computed on this frame (reading a: on its x1.5 version). The fold leaves the mid unchanged up to the last bit of floating point.
readings_of_open_details.L3_calendar: Candidate evenings: New York dates E from Monday to Thursday, 2013-01-01 to 2021-12-30. Skipped, first reason counted: E from 24 December to 1 January inclusive; E an NYSE full holiday; E+1 one (idxus_lib.us_holidays(year)[0] minus SPECIAL_CLOSURES: 2018-12-05 is a normal day; half days are normal days). Result 1,753 evenings, 2013-01-02 to 2021-12-22 (48 / 52 / 26 Monday-Thursday dates skipped by these reasons). Clock times are New York wall clock (America/New_York, tz database); no daylight-saving switch falls on a Monday-Thursday evening.
readings_of_open_details.L4_tradable_evenings: A calendar evening is tradable for a cross when at least 480 H1 bars of that cross are completed at 17:15 New York (goldlab.data.bars(base, '1h'), start + 60 min <= 17:15), counted from the frame's first bar (2013-01-01 22:00 UTC or a few minutes later). There is no per-evening quote test: missing minutes act through the band's span rule, the 5-minute entry rule and exit_index.
readings_of_open_details.L5_coverage: Before the run (precheck.json), a cross with at least one M1 bar starting in [17:15, 21:00) New York (merged frame, timestamps only) on fewer than 90 % of the 1,753 calendar evenings is dropped; declared.json lists the crosses kept. With crosses dropped, the basket bars use the crosses kept: crosses with a positive expectancy >= 65 % of the kept crosses rounded up (8 of 12 when none is dropped); the 25 % share bar is unchanged.
readings_of_open_details.L6_bars: Signal bars: goldlab.data.bars(frame, '5min') ('15min' for m15), clock buckets on the UTC grid (the New York grid: its offsets are whole hours), labelled by their start, a bucket with no M1 bar has no bar; mid close = (bc + ac) / 2 of the bucket's last M1 bar; bar end = bucket start + bar length (not goldlab's t_close); C = ac - bc of the bucket's last M1 bar. H1 bars: goldlab.data.bars(frame, '1h'), mid high = (max bh + max ah) / 2, mid low = (min bl + min al) / 2, range = mid high - mid low, hours with no M1 bar absent.
readings_of_open_details.L7_band: For signal bar j: the 20 existing bars j-19 .. j (positions among existing bars, the signal bar included); mu = their mean, sigma = their population standard deviation (ddof 0), both from plain sequential sums over exactly these 20 values (so a band depends only on its 20 closes: truncation test, hand check). Usable only if bar j-19 starts at or after (end of bar j) - 120 minutes (360 for m15); fewer than 20 bars: not usable. Bands mu +/- band_k x sigma.
readings_of_open_details.L8_decisions: Decision times t_k = 17:15 + k x 5 minutes New York on E, k = 0..32 (main: 17:15 .. 19:55, 33 a night; first_hour 9: 17:15 .. 17:55; m15: 17:15 + 15k, k = 0..10, to 19:45). The signal bar is the bar of the bucket [t_k - bar length, t_k); no bar, or a band not usable: no signal.
readings_of_open_details.L9_signal: Strict: buy if close < mu - band_k x sigma, sell if close > mu + band_k x sigma (band_k 2.0; 2.5 in width_2.5); equality is no signal, so sigma = 0 never signals. D = |close - mu|.
readings_of_open_details.L10_cost_filter: The signal is kept only if D >= 2.0 x C (equality kept), C of the frame the orders are built on (base: Dukascopy spread + c x mid; reading a: 1.5 x that).
readings_of_open_details.L11_entry: Entry bar = the first M1 bar starting at or after t_k (goldlab.data.entry_index; a bar starting at t_k has delay 0). Dropped if there is none or it starts more than 5 minutes after t_k (exactly 5 is kept), or if its open already reached the target (buy: ask open >= mu; sell: bid open <= mu; quotes of the frame the orders are built on). A dropped order does not block later signals. Fill = goldlab.sim market entry (etype 0): ask open x (1 + 0.1 x 1e-4) for a buy, bid open x (1 - 0.1 x 1e-4) for a sell.
readings_of_open_details.L12_target: Target = mu of the signal bar, frozen as an absolute price (goldlab.sim 'target'): a resting limit without slippage, filled at the target, or at a better open when a later bar gaps through it (engine rule), possibly on the entry bar; stop first when stop and target are both touched in one bar (engine rule).
readings_of_open_details.L13_stop: Stop distance = 2.0 (3.0 in stop_3.0) x the mean range of the 480 most recent H1 bars completed at the DECISION time t_k (start + 60 min <= t_k), set from the fill (goldlab.sim stop_dist) and fixed; filled at the stop with 0.3 bp of slippage, or at the worse open on a gap (engine rule). An order with a stop distance <= 0 is dropped (counted; none expected).
readings_of_open_details.L14_time_exit: exit_i = goldlab.data.exit_index(frame, 21:00 New York of E, max_gap_min=30): the first bar starting at or after 21:00 if it starts at most 30 minutes after it, else the last bar before 21:00; a market exit with 0.1 bp. An order whose exit bar is not after its entry bar is dropped (counted; none expected), as Addendum K did.
readings_of_open_details.L15_positions: goldlab.sim.simulate per cross with no_overlap=True: orders sorted by entry bar; an order whose entry bar is at or before the open trade's exit bar is skipped (no queue, no reversal, no adding); later orders of the evening trade on either side; crosses are independent; no cap across crosses or currencies (reported).
readings_of_open_details.L16_swap_and_clock_asserts: Engine swap rates are 0. Asserted on every trade (common.check_trades): entry and exit in one trading day (goldlab.data.trading_day), the day E+1 its evening opens, so no 17:00 New York rollover is crossed and the swap is 0; entry at or after 17:15 and by 20:00 New York (20:05 for null replays, which may enter 5 minutes after a 20:00 clock time); exit by 21:30 New York; swap column 0; no end-of-data exit.
readings_of_open_details.L17_R: R = goldlab.sim pnl / risk = side x (exit fill - entry fill) / |entry fill - stop| (the engine's commission is 0 because the commission is in the quotes; swap 0).
readings_of_open_details.L18_costs_x1.5: Frame = goldlab.sim.apply_spread_mult(base, 1.5) (each bar's close spread, commission included, x 1.5 around the mid, applied to its four prices: the lab's transform); slippage x 1.5 (0.15 bp market, 0.45 bp stop). Reading a: orders rebuilt on that frame: the filter sees 1.5 C and the refused-target check uses the widened open; the bands use the same mid closes up to the last bit, while the H1 ranges (and so the stop distances) are recomputed on the widened quotes and differ from the base frame's when the spread varies inside the hour (each minute is widened by its own close spread, so the bid and ask extremes can move by different amounts; Addendum K's attack found the same, I1). Reading b: the base order frame replayed through the same simulate call (no_overlap=True) on the widened frame, so the one-position rule acts on the stressed exits; fills already past the target follow the engine's first-bar rule and are counted. Bar: pooled PF >= 1.04 in both.
readings_of_open_details.L19_gross: The base order frame replayed on goldlab.sim.apply_spread_mult(base, 0.0) (each bar's close spread removed around the mid on its four prices: the lab's 'gross' frame of r2.run, which Addendum K called mid quotes; the open, high and low are the mid only where their own spread equals the close spread) with zero slippage, no_overlap=True: the gross bp of the base reading and of reading b (the same orders). Reading a's gross bp comes from its OWN rebuilt orders replayed the same way on the same gross frame (reading 'gross_a'), so every reading's cost bp is the gross bp of its own orders minus its net bp. Information only.
readings_of_open_details.L20_every_signal: Every order of the configuration (after the filters and entry checks, before the one-position rule), base costs, goldlab.sim.simulate no_overlap=False. Judged on the main only.
readings_of_open_details.L21_moving_mid: The main's orders (same drops) without a resting target; exit_i = min(21:00 exit bar, the first M1 bar starting at or after the end of the first usable M5 bar whose end is after the entry bar's start and whose mid close is >= (long) / <= (short) its own middle band); equality counts; with no such bar, the 21:00 exit. No gap rule applies to this moving exit: the text gives the 30-minute rule to the 21:00 exit only (which keeps it), and a 'last bar before' would take the exit price at the open of a minute whose own close is the trigger, before the exit signal exists. The exit bar therefore always starts at or after the trigger bar's end, which is after the entry bar's start, so it is always after the entry bar. Stop and 21:00 exit unchanged. These exits are counted apart (exit kind 'moving_mid', L30).
readings_of_open_details.L22_one_per_night: The earliest order (smallest decision time) of each cross and evening among the main's orders after all filters and entry checks; the later orders of that evening are not sent (status 'not_first_order_of_evening').
readings_of_open_details.L23_m15: goldlab.data.bars(frame, '15min'), band period 20, span limit 360 minutes, decisions at the ends of the 15-minute buckets 17:15 .. 19:45 (11); C from the M15 bucket's last M1 bar; filter, entry, H1 stop and 21:00 exit unchanged.
readings_of_open_details.L24_other_neighbours: first_hour changes only the last decision (17:55: 9 decisions); width_2.5 only band_k (2.5); stop_3.0 only the stop multiple (3.0). first_hour's and one_per_night's orders are exact subsets of the main's orders.
readings_of_open_details.L25_drop_order: Counted in this order, the first failed test of a decision wins: no signal bar; band not usable; no band crossing; cost filter; entry more than 5 minutes late (or no bar); open already at the target; stop distance <= 0; exit bar not after the entry bar; (one_per_night: not the first order of the evening); then the engine's one-position skip.
readings_of_open_details.L26_criteria: Main only, base costs unless stated: n = pooled trades >= 250; PF on R (sum of positive R / |sum of negative R|; no trade 0; no loss inf) >= 1.12; t = mean / (sd ddof 1 / sqrt(days)) of the daily sums of R per goldlab.trading_day(entry_time), days with a trade, >= 2.5; at least 6 of the 9 UTC entry years 2013-2021 with sum R > 0 (a year without a trade is not positive); pooled PF >= 1.04 in reading a AND reading b; crosses with mean R > 0 (no trade = not positive) >= ceil(0.65 x crosses kept) = 8 of 12; max over crosses of (cross sum R / pooled sum R) <= 0.25, a pooled sum <= 0 fails; numpy median of the six neighbours' pooled base PFs >= 1.06; every-signal expectancy > 0; max hold <= 192 h (goldlab.r2.is_criteria's 5 trading days); null percentile >= 97.5; |weekly rho with the sum of the ten| <= 0.30. Pass = all twelve. Every bar is read on the UNROUNDED figure ('<name>_raw' in run.json: pf, t_daily, expectancy_R, total_R, max_cross_share, max_hold_h; 'percentile_raw' in null.json; 'corr_with_sum_of_ten_raw' in correlation.json; the neighbours' median of their unrounded PFs); the rounded figures are for display only.

criteria.n>=250: pooled trades of the main at base costs >= 250

criteria.years_pos>=6/9: at least 6 of the 9 UTC entry years 2013-2021 with sum R > 0 (no trade = not positive)
criteria.stress_pf>=1.04_both_readings: pooled PF >= 1.04 at costs x1.5 in reading a (rebuilt) and in reading b (same orders)
criteria.crosses_positive: crosses with mean R > 0 >= ceil(0.65 x crosses kept) (8 of 12; no trade = not positive)
criteria.max_cross_share<=25%: no cross above 25 % of the pooled net R; a pooled total <= 0 fails
criteria.neighbours_median_pf>=1.06: median of the six neighbours' pooled base PFs >= 1.06
criteria.every_signal_exp>0: mean R of every order of the main (overlaps allowed, base costs) > 0
criteria.max_hold<=5_trading_days: longest hold of the main <= 192 h
criteria.null>=97.5pct: share of the 200 null replay means strictly below the main's pooled mean R >= 97.5 %
criteria.abs_weekly_corr_with_ten<=0.30: |Pearson rho| of the weekly R with the sum of the ten (418 weeks) <= 0.30
